text.arabic_uthmani: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ لَا تَتَّخِذُوا۟ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱتَّخَذُوا۟ دِينَكُمْ هُزُوًۭا وَلَعِبًۭا مِّنَ ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُوا۟ ٱلْكِتَٰبَ مِن قَبْلِكُمْ وَٱلْكُفَّارَ أَوْلِيَآءَ ۚ وَٱتَّقُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ إِن كُنتُم مُّؤْمِنِينَ

words.gloss_range: vocative particle opening a direct legal address
words.prose: {{ar:يَا}} ({{tr:yā}}) opens the ayah by calling the audience into direct legal speech. The later plural markers remain continuous with this summons, so the prohibition is not abstract advice but addressed obligation.

topics.headline: vocative summons opens a legal address
topics.summary: Covers 6 CRITICAL rows for this word.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah is heard first as a direct summons, so the prohibition arrives as addressed obligation rather than detached rule.
topics.reason: The rows converge on the opening call establishing second-person legal address, audience continuity, and command-register pacing.

words.gloss_range: formal vocative element that alerts and prepares the specified addressee class
words.prose: {{ar:أَيُّهَا}} ({{tr:ayyuhā}}) stretches the call with an alerting vocative form and waits for the relative clause to specify the audience. The form both widens the summons across the community and presses each listener into the identity being named, turning the collective declared in 5:56 into direct practical address.

topics.headline: alerting vocative specifies who is summoned
topics.summary: Covers 5 CRITICAL rows for this word.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the call is both ceremonially alerting and narrowing: each addressee is pressed to locate himself inside the believing class.
topics.reason: The rows support a formal vocative whose alerting force and following relative clause define the summoned group.

topics.headline: declared collective becomes directly addressed
topics.summary: Covers 1 CRITICAL rows for this word.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the handoff from the prior declared party to practical obligation in this ayah.
topics.reason: The boundary row gives a coherent same-surah transition from collective declaration to second-person command.

words.gloss_range: relative pronoun defining the addressed group by the following faith clause
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلَّذِينَ}} ({{tr:alladhīna}}) defines the addressed group through the following faith verb rather than through tribe or title. Its later repetitions for other groups make conduct and reception the ayah’s grammar of identity.

topics.headline: relative clauses define communities by conduct
topics.summary: Covers 5 CRITICAL rows for this word.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that group identity in the ayah is built through relative clauses: believers, mockers, and scripture-recipients are distinguished by what they have done or received.
topics.reason: The rows all support the relative pronoun as an identity-forming device, including the threefold local reprise.

words.gloss_range: perfect Form IV plural faith/trust verb used as prior addressee identity
words.root_gloss_range: security, trust, faith, and giving safety; locally selected as completed entry into faith/trust identity
words.prose: {{ar:ءَامَنُوا۟}} ({{tr:āmanū}}) presents the addressees as those who have already entered faith and trust before any prohibition is spoken. That identity carries security-pressure from the root field, but locally it functions as the audience label whose reality will be tested again at the closing participle.

topics.headline: perfect objectless faith names prior identity
topics.summary: Covers 5 CRITICAL rows for this word.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that faith is already the audience label before the prohibition begins, and the rule tests that claimed identity.
topics.reason: QAC and valency evidence support a perfect Form IV verb used objectlessly as the relative-clause identity of the addressees.

topics.headline: security and trust pressure enrich the faith label
topics.summary: Covers 7 CRITICAL rows for this word.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the faith label carries security and trust pressure, while local grammar keeps it as the addressee identity rather than a separate safety-giving act.
topics.reason: The root evidence supports trust and safety pressure, but the local Form IV clause selects completed belief or trust identity.

topics.headline: opening faith returns as a closing test
topics.summary: Covers 10 CRITICAL rows for this word.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the ayah as a faith ring: the opening completed claim is tested by the closing ongoing believer-state.
topics.reason: The remaining rows support the same-surah legal-address formula, the ʾ-m-n bookend, and the shift from membership statement to obligation.

words.gloss_range: prohibitive particle governing the following jussive adoption verb
words.prose: {{ar:لَا}} ({{tr:lā}}) turns the opened identity-frame into prohibition. Its force governs the coming jussive verb and the full delayed complement, so the ban covers the role-assignment as a whole; the formula also recalls the alliance prohibition of 5:51.

topics.headline: prohibitive particle governs the full adoption clause
topics.summary: Covers 3 CRITICAL rows for this word.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ban reaches the whole take-as construction, including the delayed role complement, not merely the first named people.
topics.reason: The rows identify the particle as prohibitive and jussive-governing, with scope over the double-object adoption frame.

topics.headline: short negation pivots from identity into law
topics.summary: Covers 2 CRITICAL rows for this word.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the abrupt move from extended believing address to a clipped legal prohibition, with a same-surah echo of 5:51.
topics.reason: The placement and 5:51 formula row support the particle as a structural and inter-ayah pivot.

words.gloss_range: prohibited Form VIII adoption verb with a double-object frame
words.root_gloss_range: taking, grasping, seizing, and adopting; locally selected as deliberate Form VIII taking-for-oneself
words.prose: {{ar:تَتَّخِذُوا۟}} ({{tr:tattakhidhū}}) controls the main prohibition as a double-object verb: the addressees must not take the described people as awliyāʾ. Form VIII makes the taking deliberate and self-directed, and the verb is placed so their forbidden adoption would mirror the mockers’ completed adoption of dīn as ridicule.

topics.headline: double-object verb bans assigning a role
topics.summary: Covers 6 CRITICAL rows for this word.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the issue is not contact alone but assigning the described people the role of awliyāʾ.
topics.reason: Grammar and valency rows make the verb double-transitive and show the delayed role complement as essential.

topics.headline: Form VIII makes taking deliberate and self-directed
topics.summary: Covers 6 CRITICAL rows for this word.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices voluntary adoption for oneself rather than unavoidable coexistence; the forbidden act is chosen allegiance formation.
topics.reason: Root and form rows support grasping/taking narrowed into Form VIII deliberate adoption.

topics.headline: believers’ taking mirrors mockers’ taking
topics.summary: Covers 10 CRITICAL rows for this word.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the structural irony: believers must not answer the mockers’ completed taking of dīn with their own taking of the mockers as patrons.
topics.reason: The remaining rows support the 5:51 and 5:58 echoes, the adoption-alliance pair, and the internal mirror between the two taking verbs.

words.gloss_range: relative pronoun functioning as the first object of the prohibited adoption
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلَّذِينَ}} ({{tr:alladhīna}}) is the first object of the prohibited adoption, not a new subject. The same relative form that defined the believers now defines the forbidden group, making conduct rather than grammar separate the two sides.

topics.headline: second relative pronoun names the prohibited object
topics.summary: Covers 5 CRITICAL rows for this word.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the same relative form now points away from the believers toward the people they must not adopt, sharpening the inside/outside divide.
topics.reason: The rows all support word 7 as the first object of the prohibition and as a role-reversing reprise of the earlier relative pronoun.

words.gloss_range: perfect Form VIII adoption verb describing completed reclassification by the mockers
words.root_gloss_range: taking, grasping, seizing, and adopting; locally selected as completed Form VIII reclassification
words.prose: {{ar:ٱتَّخَذُوا۟}} ({{tr:ittakhadhū}}) names the mockers’ completed act: they have taken the community’s dīn and assigned it the status of ridicule and play. The same Form VIII taking echoes word 6, so the ayah warns the believers not to mirror people whose own taking has already degraded sacred obligation; the pattern also resonates with dīn-as-play contexts in 6:70 and 7:51 and with the immediate repetition in 5:58.

topics.headline: completed taking reclassifies dīn as ridicule
topics.summary: Covers 6 CRITICAL rows for this word.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the mockers’ act is presented as accomplished reclassification: dīn is made to count as mockery and play.
topics.reason: The grammar rows support a perfect double-object verb whose complements name the degraded result-status.

topics.headline: same Form VIII contrasts their settled act with your blocked act
topics.summary: Covers 6 CRITICAL rows for this word.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the paired taking verbs: their completed taking becomes the reason your taking must not begin.
topics.reason: The form and echo rows support the internal contrast between completed third-person taking and prohibited second-person taking.

topics.headline: take-as-dīn formula joins a wider mockery pattern
topics.summary: Covers 3 CRITICAL rows for this word.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that 5:57 is not an isolated phrasing; it belongs to a Quranic pattern of treating dīn or worship as play, including 6:70, 7:51, and the immediate echo in 5:58.
topics.reason: The remaining rows give concrete formula parallels and same-surah links that preserve the mockery-pattern payoff.

words.gloss_range: possessed abstract noun naming the addressed community’s obligation and way of life
words.root_gloss_range: debt, judgment, accountability, obedience, and way of life; locally the possessed obligation-system being trivialized
words.prose: {{ar:دِينَكُمْ}} ({{tr:dīnakum}}) is the possessed object that the mockers reclassify. The suffix makes the target communal, and the dīn field keeps obligation, accountability, and way of life in view, so the degradation is not merely insult but a stripping of weight from the believers’ own binding order. That threat stands against same-surah pressure points where dīn is completed (5:3), abandoned (5:54), and guarded from excess (5:77).

topics.headline: possessed dīn is the object being reclassified
topics.summary: Covers 7 CRITICAL rows for this word.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the mockery is aimed at the believers’ own communal obligation-system, not at an abstract label detached from them.
topics.reason: Grammar and suffix rows support dīn as the first object of the completed taking and as possessed by the addressed community.

topics.headline: debt and accountability pressure make the degradation sharper
topics.summary: Covers 10 CRITICAL rows for this word.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that what is trivialized includes obligation, reckoning, and lived order, while local usage still selects the community’s dīn as the object.
topics.reason: The semantic rows support debt, judgment, and way-of-life pressure without replacing the local possessed noun sense.

topics.headline: same-surah dīn pressure points frame the threat
topics.summary: Covers 4 CRITICAL rows for this word.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the mocked dīn stands against same-surah moments of completed dīn, apostasy from dīn, and warning against excess in dīn at 5:3, 5:54, and 5:77.
topics.reason: The remaining rows give the same-surah and dīn-kitāb network that makes mockery a legal and identity threat.

words.gloss_range: accusative gerund naming ridicule as a result-status assigned to dīn
words.root_gloss_range: ridicule, derision, and emptying weight from a serious matter; locally applied to dīn as degradation
words.prose: {{ar:هُزُوًۭا}} ({{tr:huzuwan}}) gives the first degraded result-status assigned to dīn. It is ridicule as hollowing-out of seriousness, and its pairing with play forms a tight formula repeated in 5:58 and echoed in dīn-play contexts at 6:70 and 7:51; variant hamza forms add recitational texture without changing the local sense.

topics.headline: ridicule is a result-status for dīn
topics.summary: Covers 7 CRITICAL rows for this word.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that ridicule is what dīn is made into; the word names an emptying of seriousness, not harmless laughter.
topics.reason: The grammar and semantic rows support huzuwan as result complement, with a live circumstantial shade that does not displace the transformation reading.

topics.headline: ridicule joins play in a tight formula
topics.summary: Covers 8 CRITICAL rows for this word.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the paired degradation formula that recurs immediately in 5:58 and in wider dīn-play contexts.
topics.reason: The formula, recurrence, and distribution rows support huzuwan as the first member of a constrained mockery-play pair.

topics.headline: variant hamza forms expose sound pressure without changing sense
topics.summary: Covers 3 CRITICAL rows for this word.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices recitational pressure inside the ridicule word, while the local meaning remains mockery.
topics.reason: Accepted variant rows are useful as apparatus and phonetic pressure, but they do not alter the local referent or govern the parse.

words.gloss_range: coordinating particle joining the two accusative degradation terms
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) coordinates the two accusative degradation terms. It keeps ridicule and play distinct while binding them into one formulaic pair.

topics.headline: wa keeps ridicule and play coordinate
topics.summary: Covers 5 CRITICAL rows for this word.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah does not collapse ridicule and play into one vague idea; the connector holds two equal modes of trivialization together.
topics.reason: All rows support coordination of the two accusative gerunds and the cadence created between them.

words.gloss_range: coordinated accusative gerund naming play as a second degradation term
words.root_gloss_range: play, amusement, purposeless activity, and suspension of consequence; locally a result-status assigned to dīn
words.prose: {{ar:لَعِبًۭا}} ({{tr:laʿiban}}) completes the degradation pair as a second accusative complement. It names purposeless play against the accountability of dīn, and its recurrence with huzuwan in 5:58 turns the pair into a recognizable two-beat pattern rather than a casual flourish; the vowel variant remains apparatus and does not change the local role.

topics.headline: play completes the result-complement pair
topics.summary: Covers 4 CRITICAL rows for this word.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that play is not decorative; it occupies the same grammatical result slot as ridicule.
topics.reason: Grammar rows support laʿiban as coordinated accusative complement inherited through wa.

topics.headline: play cancels consequence against dīn
topics.summary: Covers 4 CRITICAL rows for this word.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the semantic collision: dīn carries accountability while play suspends purpose and consequence.
topics.reason: The semantic rows support play as the antithesis of accountable order in this local pairing.

topics.headline: formula recurrence and variant form complete the pair
topics.summary: Covers 9 CRITICAL rows for this word.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the repeated two-beat formula, while the vowel variant remains apparatus and does not change the local role.
topics.reason: The remaining rows support the dīn-play formula, the immediate 5:58 echo, shared gerund cadence, and a non-semantic variant.

words.gloss_range: preposition opening a source or explanatory specification of the forbidden group
words.prose: {{ar:مِنَ}} ({{tr:mina}}) begins the specification of the forbidden group. Its partitive or explanatory range matters because the syntax can make the Book-recipients a subset within the mockers or an explanatory identity for them, while the sentence delays the patronage role until the specification is heard.

topics.headline: min opens a consequential group-specification
topics.summary: Covers 6 CRITICAL rows for this word.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a real scope question: the phrase may mark a subset from the Book-recipients or explain who the mockers are, and the delayed awliyāʾ role waits until that specification is complete.
topics.reason: The rows support both partitive and explanatory values, plus the insertion of a long specification before the delayed complement.

words.gloss_range: genitive relative pronoun governed by the preceding preposition
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلَّذِينَ}} ({{tr:alladhīna}}) is governed by the preceding preposition and begins the scripture-recipient specification. Unlike the earlier action-defined groups, this relative clause defines its group by reception, completing the ayah’s layered identity architecture.

topics.headline: third relative clause marks scripture-reception identity
topics.summary: Covers 5 CRITICAL rows for this word.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the third relative clause is governed inside the min-phrase and defines a group by what they received, not by a new action they initiate here.
topics.reason: The rows support a genitive relative pronoun after min and complete the three-layer identity architecture.

words.gloss_range: passive perfect Form IV verb foregrounding received scripture status
words.root_gloss_range: coming, bringing, and giving; locally the passive caused-reception of scripture
words.prose: {{ar:أُوتُوا۟}} ({{tr:ūtū}}) is passive perfect, so the wording foregrounds the recipients’ status as those given scripture rather than their achievement. That recurring given-the-Book designation is real, but the ayah places it inside the mockery boundary: a granted Book-status does not by itself make someone a legitimate patron.

topics.headline: passive verb foregrounds recipient status
topics.summary: Covers 9 CRITICAL rows for this word.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the group’s status rests on a received grant, yet that status does not exempt them from exclusion when dīn is mocked.
topics.reason: Grammar and passive rows foreground reception of scripture while suppressing the giver in the verb.

topics.headline: given-the-Book formula places them in a wider category
topics.summary: Covers 5 CRITICAL rows for this word.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a technical Quranic designation for previous scripture-holders, now placed under the alliance boundary.
topics.reason: The remaining rows support the recurrent ūtū al-kitāb formula and its measured cadence.

words.gloss_range: definite scripture noun received under the passive giving verb
words.root_gloss_range: writing, inscription, prescription, and binding order; locally the recognized Book granted to prior recipients
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْكِتَٰبَ}} ({{tr:al-kitāba}}) completes the passive reception frame as the definite, recognized Book. Its root field supports written and binding authority, and its placement near dīn and kuffār sharpens the contrast between received disclosure and concealment or trivialization.

topics.headline: the definite Book carries written and binding authority
topics.summary: Covers 9 CRITICAL rows for this word.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the received object is recognized scripture with binding authority, while local grammar keeps it as the object of the passive reception verb.
topics.reason: The rows support the definite Book as received object, with writing/prescription and stitching/joining pressure narrowed to binding authority.

topics.headline: scripture reception contrasts concealment and obligation
topics.summary: Covers 6 CRITICAL rows for this word.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that codified disclosure stands near dīn and kuffār, making mockery by scripture-recipients especially marked.
topics.reason: The remaining rows preserve the reception-vs-identity framing, same-surah Book texture, and contrast with concealment.

words.gloss_range: preposition marking temporal anteriority with the following adverb
words.prose: {{ar:مِنْ}} ({{tr:min}}) shifts the repeated particle into temporal work. Unlike word 13, it governs the before-you phrase and places the scripture-recipients prior to the addressed community.

topics.headline: second min marks temporal before-you relation
topics.summary: Covers 6 CRITICAL rows for this word.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the repeated particle changes function: the earlier min specifies source, while this one locates the Book-recipients before the addressed community.
topics.reason: All rows support temporal governance with qablikum and an internal contrast with the earlier min; the boundary row links the command to the prior allegiance logic.

words.gloss_range: temporal adverb with a plural suffix anchoring prior communities before the addressees
words.root_gloss_range: before, facing, precedence, and acceptance; locally temporal before-you precedence with facing-precedent pressure
words.prose: {{ar:قَبْلِكُمْ}} ({{tr:qablikum}}) closes the scripture-recipient phrase by anchoring them before the addressed believers. The root’s facing/frontness pressure makes that past group stand as a precedent, but the local construction remains temporal: prior reception does not override the alliance boundary.

topics.headline: before-you fixes prior scripture recipients against the addressees
topics.summary: Covers 6 CRITICAL rows for this word.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that prior scripture status is measured relative to the believers being addressed, so history becomes a direct precedent for their alliance choices.
topics.reason: Grammar and suffix rows support temporal precedence anchored to the addressees.

topics.headline: before also carries facing-precedent pressure
topics.summary: Covers 4 CRITICAL rows for this word.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the prior community stands before the addressees as a precedent, while local syntax keeps the primary sense temporal.
topics.reason: The q-b-l field allows facing/frontness pressure, but min plus qablikum fixes temporal anteriority locally.

topics.headline: qabl links the prohibition to prior-community memory
topics.summary: Covers 3 CRITICAL rows for this word.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that precedence is acknowledged but does not authorize walāya when mockery is present.
topics.reason: The remaining rows preserve qabl-kitāb pairing and same-surah prior-community memory.

words.gloss_range: coordinator introducing the kuffār term with live scope consequences
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) adds the kuffār term while leaving coordination scope consequential. It can be heard with the Book-recipient specification or with the broader prohibited object field, and the following case evidence exposes that tension.

topics.headline: wa adds kuffār with live attachment scope
topics.summary: Covers 5 CRITICAL rows for this word.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the coordinator does not simply add a flat label; it leaves open whether kuffār are routed under the min-phrase or as a parallel prohibited category.
topics.reason: All rows support coordination with structural ambiguity that becomes consequential at word 20.

words.gloss_range: definite intensive plural naming persistent concealers or deniers
words.root_gloss_range: covering, concealment, denial, and ingratitude; locally an intensive plural category disqualified from walāya
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْكُفَّارَ}} ({{tr:al-kuffāra}}) lands just before the delayed awliyāʾ complement as the broad concealment category, widening the alliance prohibition beyond the named groups of 5:51. Its intensive plural form marks persistent covering or denial, and variant case evidence narrows how far the coordination can route syntactically while the canonical surface remains accusative.

topics.headline: case variation exposes two group maps
topics.summary: Covers 9 CRITICAL rows for this word.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that accusative and genitive routing change the syntax of the group map, while the canonical local surface keeps the word as accusative.
topics.reason: Case and variant rows are valid apparatus for scope, but canonical accusative governs the local parse.

topics.headline: intensive plural marks persistent concealment
topics.summary: Covers 10 CRITICAL rows for this word.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the category is not a casual plural but a hardened concealment/denial identity, sharpened beside the Book’s disclosure.
topics.reason: Semantic and form rows support kuffār as an intensive plural of persistent covering, denial, and ingratitude.

topics.headline: same-surah field broadens the alliance prohibition
topics.summary: Covers 5 CRITICAL rows for this word.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices movement from named groups in 5:51 toward a broader conduct-and-concealment category in 5:57.
topics.reason: The remaining rows connect k-f-r with walāya, same-surah denial, and the delayed awliyāʾ complement.

words.gloss_range: delayed plural role complement naming protectors, patrons, or authority-allies
words.root_gloss_range: nearness, succession, protection, authority, and allegiance; locally a forbidden patronage role
words.prose: {{ar:أَوْلِيَآءَ}} ({{tr:awliyāʾa}}) finally names the role the described people must not receive. The word is not thin friendship here; it carries nearness, protection, patronage, and authority, and it completes the same-surah walāya argument by excluding from that role the people who mock dīn or conceal disclosure after proper walāya has been defined and declared in 5:55-5:56.

topics.headline: awliyāʾ resolves the long double-object construction
topics.summary: Covers 9 CRITICAL rows for this word.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the sentence withholds the forbidden role until after the group has been fully specified, making patronage the decisive complement.
topics.reason: Grammar and structure rows support awliyāʾ as the delayed second object of tattakhidhū.

topics.headline: walāya combines nearness, protection, and authority
topics.summary: Covers 4 CRITICAL rows for this word.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ban targets authority-bearing closeness and patronage, while local syntax keeps it as the role complement of taking.
topics.reason: The semantic rows support nearness/protection/governance pressure and narrow away a thin friendship-only gloss.

topics.headline: proper walāya frames forbidden awliyāʾ
topics.summary: Covers 8 CRITICAL rows for this word.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that 5:55-5:56 define proper allegiance, while 5:57 excludes mockers and kuffār from that same role.
topics.reason: The remaining rows preserve the same-surah walāya sequence and the immediate 5:58 example anticipated by the mockery criterion.

words.gloss_range: resumptive conjunction pivoting from prohibition to positive command
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) resumes with a new command rather than adding another object. It pivots the ayah from forbidden patronage to the positive protective action that follows.

topics.headline: resumptive wa pivots from avoidance to protection
topics.summary: Covers 5 CRITICAL rows for this word.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah does not end with avoidance; the connector opens a fresh positive command after the prohibition.
topics.reason: All rows support resumptive rather than object-coordinating force, marking a new imperative clause.

words.gloss_range: plural imperative Form VIII command of God-directed self-shielding
words.root_gloss_range: protection, guarding, and shielding; locally an imperative of reflexive God-directed protection
words.prose: {{ar:ٱتَّقُوا۟}} ({{tr:ittaqū}}) begins the positive command after the prohibition. Its w-q-y field gives a shielding payoff: the believers are not merely told to avoid bad allegiance but to build God-directed protection, a rival self-directed act against the taking verbs that dominate the middle of the ayah.

topics.headline: imperative commands God-directed protection
topics.summary: Covers 5 CRITICAL rows for this word.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the command after the ban is active and God-directed, not generic caution.
topics.reason: Grammar rows support an imperative Form VIII verb governing the divine name and opening the closing command unit.

topics.headline: taqwā is active self-shielding
topics.summary: Covers 6 CRITICAL rows for this word.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a shield image: believers are told to interpose God-directed protection against the alliance danger just named.
topics.reason: The w-q-y root and Form VIII rows support active self-shielding, while the local object keeps the command God-directed.

topics.headline: self-shielding answers self-directed adoption
topics.summary: Covers 8 CRITICAL rows for this word.
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the antidote structure: the ayah replaces wrong self-directed adoption with God-directed self-shielding.
topics.reason: The remaining rows connect ittaqū with same-surah legal commands, ʾ-m-n identity, and the rival Form VIII taking verbs.

words.gloss_range: proper divine name as the object of the protective command
words.root_gloss_range: deity, worship-orientation, and divine authority; locally the fixed proper name as object of taqwā

topics.headline: the divine name anchors the protective command

baseline_models.mechanism: The targets are identified by what they do to دينكم: installing such actors as close norm-setters gives purposeless treatment of communal obedience a formative place inside the believing group.

activation_trace.role: Making or acquiring something for oneself supplies the deliberate installation step in the relation.

Action without a sound intended end supplies the deforming stance toward that enacted order.

context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies intragroup partition, positive nearness and affection, and receptive recognition; I infer that the relative clause in 5:57 behaviorally narrows the target and blocks a blanket ban on benign relations. surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it derives institutional custody from lexical recurrence rather than an explicit office in 5:57. It remains anchored in the focus's double taking, دين as obedience, and awliya as charge over affairs, while 5:70 joins taking to a binding covenant. Render it as an exploratory account of formative authority, not as a replacement gloss for awliya or as a ban on every relation.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The focus opposes two acts of taking around religion and awliya; the later أخذنا ميثاق supplies covenantal custody as a third act of taking.

activation_trace.role: Deliberate acquisition connects the two focus acts and permits an exploratory custody reading.
Obedience gives the object of custody an enacted communal form.
Charge over an affair supplies the institutional role into which an actor may be installed.
God's taking of the covenant activates possession as solemn custody rather than casual association.
The confirmed covenant supplies the binding object whose mediation can be entrusted or betrayed.

changed_reading.before: The verse regulates friendship with religious mockers.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, it regulates custody of covenant-shaped communal obedience: do not install its trivializers as the people charged with mediating and guarding it.

strongest_changes: The immediate prayer-call reprise turns generic mockery into disruption of an audible, gathering public practice.
The later failure of restraint and exact 5:80-81 wilayah reprise make normative governance and conflict transmission central senses of the prohibited relation.
The internal distinctions of 5:66 and the positive closeness, affection, and recognition of 5:82-83 block a blanket category-based social reading.
summary.what_was_special: The packet repeatedly reuses the focus's roots and constructions but then places condemned wilayah beside positive qurb and wudd. That sequence preserves a firm allegiance boundary while sharply distinguishing formative authority from ordinary or receptive intercommunal closeness.
remaining_uncertainties: The exact boundary among intimate friendship, political alliance, patronage, and governing authority remains polysemous in awliya.
The divine-protection inference may be specific to the messenger rather than a general rule for all believers.
The covenant-custody model is traceable but remains an exploratory institutional extension of the repeated taking motif.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **Aimless play cannot be entrusted with protective charge.** `ل ع ب B001` is action without sound aim, `ه ز ء B001` derision, and `و ل ي B003` assuming charge. The doubled “take” reverses roles: those who take religion as play must not be taken as governing allies. I infer that mockery disqualifies because it removes the stable aim protection requires.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: Later ayah 5:120 made the fixed ayah's local distinctions newly visible as bounded operations within a single encompassing dominion, rather than as an isolated rule or episode.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **Alliance with mockery imports aimlessness into the organizing relation.** Fixed **ل ع ب / B001** (“non-serious action without a sound aim”) specifies how religion is treated, while fixed **و ل ي / B004** makes the prohibited response loyal support. The prior two ayat define a party through shared orientation; 5:58 shows the prayer call itself converted into play. I infer that taking mockers as directing allies allows their aimless stance toward worship to shape one’s own collective center. The warning reads as protection of practical seriousness, not hypersensitivity to an insult alone.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadeleri bu dali yalniz korkunun kalkmasi olarak degil, kalbin yatismasi, guven verme, guvenilirlik, emanet edilen sey, guvenli yer ve dayanilir nitelik alanlariyla birlikte verir. lexicalization_scope.note: Yalin guven ve korkusuzluk anlamlari ile belirli yapimli ya da soz obegi kullanislari birlikte vardir; tanim bunlari tek bir dar kaliba indirgemez.

concept_map.definition: Korkunun kalkmasiyla kalbin yatismasi, birine guven verilmesi veya bir kimsenin ya da seyin guvenilir kabul edilmesidir. Bu alan guvenli yer, emanet edilen sey, kendisine guvenilen kisi ve dayanilir binek gibi bagimli uygulamalari da kapsar.

facets.statement: Temel cekirdek korkuya karsi guven, ic yatiskinligi ve tehlikeden emin olma halidir.
Guven verme, birini kendi koruma ve teminat alani icine alma olarak kullanilir.
Guvenilirlik, ihanete karsi sadakat, emanet edilen sey ve kendisine guvenilen kisi anlamlarini dogurur.
Guvenin bulundugu yer, bir kimsenin emniyet icinde oldugu mesken veya siginak olarak adlandirilir.
Dayanikli ve aksamasindan korkulmayan deve kullanimi, guvenilirlik niteligini canli bir ornege uygular.

يدخل فيه أخذ الأسير، والأخيذ، ومعنى وخذوهم أي ائسروهم.
يدخل فيه الأخذة رقية تأخذ العين، والتأخيذ والسحر أو الخرزة التي تحبس الرجل أو المرأة عن النكاح أو الرأي.

يدخل فيه نجوم الأخذ، وهي منازل القمر، وتسميتها لأن القمر يأخذ كل ليلة في منزل أو نوء.
يدخل فيه أخذ إخذ القوم أو أخذهم، أي السير بسيرتهم أو أخذ شكلهم وخلائقهم وهديهم.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesinin ortak çekirdeği, bir kimseyi alaya alma ve küçümseyici biçimde şaka konusu yapmadır. Gizli şaka ya da şakaya benzeyen davranış, bu çekirdeğin kaynakta açıkça belirtilen bir görünümüdür; alayın karşılığını verme, şiddetli soğuğa uğrama ve bir bineği hareket ettirme bu dalın dışında kalır.

Kişi, başkalarıyla alay eden taraf ya da başkalarının alay ettiği taraf olarak nitelenebilir.

root_profile.summary: Kök, gelme ve ulaştırmadan uygun yoldan işlemeye uzanan bir çekirdeğin yanında su yolu, dışarıdan gelen sel, yabancı kişi, ürün ve artış, mali ödeme, hayvan hareketi, yol, felaket, çiftleşme isteği ve etkili kişi gibi çoğu kalıba bağlı tarihsel anlam dalları taşır.

branches.what_is_ar: يدخل فيه أصل الجمع والضم، وخرز الأديم والسقاء، وضم شفري الدابة أو صر أخلافها، والخرزة المضمومة، واجتماع الخيل أو الكتيبة.
يدخل فيه كتب الكتاب وكتابته ونسخه، والكتاب اسما للمكتوب أو الصحيفة ذات الكتابة، والتعليم والإملاء والاستكتاب المتعلق بالكتابة.
يدخل فيه الكتاب بمعنى الفرض والحكم والقدر، والكتابة بمعنى الإثبات والتقدير والإيجاب والعزم والقضاء الممضى.

branches.branch_image_ar: إدخال الاسم في سجل أو زمرة
branches.what_is_ar: يدخل فيه الاكتتاب في الفرض والرزق، وكتابة الاسم في ديوان السلطان، ومعنى اجعلنا في زمرة الشاهدين.
يدخل فيه عقد المكاتبة بين السيد والعبد أو الأمة على مال منجم، وكتابة الشرط والنجوم المؤدية إلى العتق.

root_profile.summary: Bu kök, katma ve birleştirme çekirdeğinden yazı üretme ve yazılı ürün, bağlayıcı karar, sicile alma ve özgürlüğe götüren özel sözleşme alanlarına yayılan çok anlamlı bir yapı gösterir. Dallar bağlantılı olsa da kavram sınırları ayrı tutulmalıdır.

branches.what_is_ar: يدخل فيه الإقبال والاستقبال والمقابلة والتقابل والتجاه والعيان والقبل خلاف الدبر وجهة الأمر ووجه الجبل أو الأرض وما يقابل الحس أو النظر
يدخل فيه قبل خلاف بعد في الزمان والمكان والمنزلة والترتيب ودخول العام القابل والليلة القابلة ومن ذي قبل ومقتبل الشباب وأوائل الأمر
يدخل فيه من قبل فلان ولي قبل فلان وأصابني من قبله بمعنى من جهته أو عنده أو لدنه
يدخل فيه قبول الشيء والعذر والتوبة والهدية والعمل والتقبل والقبول الذي تقبله النفس أو العين
يدخل فيه القبلة التي يقبل الناس عليها في صلاتهم وما صار اسما للمكان المتوجه إليه للصلاة
يدخل فيه القبلة من التقبيل وفعلها قبلته تقبيلا
يدخل فيه القابلة التي تتلقى الولد عند الولادة والقابل الذي يستقبل دلو السانية أو الغرب من المستقي
يدخل فيه القبيل الكفيل والقبالة والكفالة وتقبل فلان بغيره والعهد المكتوب
يدخل فيه القبيل والقبيلة وقبائل العرب وسائر الناس والجماعات والأصناف والعريف الذي يقبل على القوم وكرم الطرفين من النسب
يدخل فيه قبائل الرأس وشعبه وقبال النعل واللجام وسيوره وقبيل الغزل ودبيره والرقاع والأحناء وما ضم بعضه إلى بعض

branches.branch_image_ar: إقبال العضو أو العلامة إلى جهة
branches.what_is_ar: يدخل فيه قبل العين وإقبال السواد على الأنف أو المحجر والقبال في الرجلين وقرنا الشاة المقبلان وشاة مقابلة قطعت أذنها من قبل وجهها

branches.what_is_ar: يدخل فيه ستر الشيء وتغطيته وكفر الدرع بثوب وتغطية السلاح والرماد المكفور وستر الشمس النجوم والسحاب الشمس
يدخل فيه الكافر للليل المظلم والبحر والنهر العظيم ومغيب الشمس وما يستر بظلمته أو سعته

يدخل فيه كفر النعمة وكفرانها وجحودها وترك شكرها والكفور في كفران النعمة
يدخل فيه الكفر بمعنى البراءة والتنصل من الشيء أو بعضهم من بعض
يدخل فيه أكفر الرجل بمعنى دعاه كافرا أو حكم بكفره أو نسبه إلى الكفر
يدخل فيه أكفرته إذا ألجأت المطيع إلى أن يعصي
يدخل فيه الكافر للزارع والكفار للزراع لأنهم يغطون الحب أو البذر بالتراب
يدخل فيه الكفارة لما يكفر الخطيئة أو اليمين والتكفير للسيئات والمعاصي حتى تصير كأن لم تعمل
يدخل فيه الكافور والكفرى والكوافير لأكمام العنب أو طلع النخل أو الورقة التي تستر الثمرة
يدخل فيه الكافور من الطيب وعين ماء في الجنة والنبات المسمى كافورا
يدخل فيه الكافر من الأرض البعيد عن الناس والكفور للقرى والكفر للقرية والقبر
يدخل فيه الكفرات والثنايا من الجبال والكفر العظيم من الجبال والحائط الواطئ
يدخل فيه التكفير بمعنى إيماء الذمي برأسه أو وضع اليد على الصدر والتطامن خضوعا
يدخل فيه التكفير بمعنى تتويج الملك بتاج أو التاج نفسه

root_mapping.policy: Use the dominant Furuq root for every QAC root, and include non-dominant Furuq targets as additional root_lexicon entries when qac-furuq-v4-root-map marks the QAC root as split.

root_lexicon.note: Turkish is the only language with dictionary entries/glosses currently sourced.
